title: Game leaderboard
summary: Real-time ranking with sorted sets and sharded scores.
prompt: Design a leaderboard for a mobile game with 50M players. Show the global top 100, a player’s own rank, and the players just above and below them, updated within seconds of a new score.

requirements: Functional: submit a score, keep each player’s best score, read the top N, a player’s rank, and nearby players.
Non-functional: rank reads in milliseconds; updates visible within seconds; scores must survive a cache loss.
Clarify: per-season or daily boards, friends-only boards, tie-breaking (assume the earlier score wins).
estimation: 50M players, 5M daily; 10 games a day each ≈ 50M score writes a day ≈ 600/s average, a few thousand per second at peak.
A sorted set entry is roughly 50–100 bytes, so 50M entries is ~2.5–5 GB: fits in memory on one node, with a replica.
Reads (opening the board) may be 10× writes; the top 100 is identical for everyone, so cache it for a second.
api: POST /scores {playerId, matchId, score} → {best, rank}; matchId makes the submission idempotent.
data: scores(player_id, season, best_score, achieved_at) in a durable database: the source of truth.
matches(match_id PK, player_id, score) to verify and deduplicate submissions.
In-memory sorted set per season: member player_id, score best_score (with a tie-break folded into the score).
design: Game servers report results to the score service, which validates them, writes the database, then updates the sorted set.
ZADD with the GT flag only raises a member’s score, so out-of-order updates cannot lower a best.
ZREVRANK gives a player’s rank in O(log N); ZREVRANGE serves the top N and a window around a rank.
deepDives: Ties: fold time into one numeric key, such as score × 2³² + (MAX_SECONDS − seconds), so earlier achievements rank higher. Sorted-set scores are 64-bit floats, so keep the combined value below 2⁵³.
Rebuild: if the sorted set is lost, rebuild it by streaming the scores table; the database stays authoritative.
Scaling past one node: shard by score range or keep approximate ranks (percentile buckets) for players far from the top, where exact rank matters less.
bottlenecks: Top-100 reads all hit one key: cache the rendered list for a second at the API layer.
Cheating: trust only server-reported results; flag impossible scores for review.
Season resets: create a new key per season instead of deleting a huge set in place.
tradeoffs: An in-memory sorted set gives exact live ranks at memory cost; a database ORDER BY with an index cannot answer “what is my rank” cheaply at this size.
Exact global rank for everyone vs approximate ranks for the long tail.
Writing the database before the cache means a crash between the two leaves the cache stale until rebuilt or re-sent; acceptable for seconds.

rubric.text: Used a structure that answers rank queries in logarithmic time.
Kept a durable source of truth and a rebuild path for the in-memory index.
Handled ties and only-increase best-score semantics.
Made score submission idempotent and server-trusted.
Sized memory for the player count.
Discussed scaling past one node: score-range sharding or approximate ranks.
